expectations.text: The reply sizes tasks rather than jobs: which tasks AI does today at the required quality, measured in a pilot against a baseline, rather than assuming 30%.
expectations.evidence: Section 3 table: 'Share of task hours AI could take at required quality: low / base / high', giving 19.0 / 29.9 / 41.2 FTE. 'The shares are assumptions from the task mix, not measurements.' Option B: 'Q1-Q2: baseline the task times, run pilots in accounts payable and reconciliations', and Gate 1 needs 'pilot hours freed against baseline, error rate no worse'. Weakness: the freed hours are gross (review time is not netted), and the base case lands almost exactly on the board's 30% at maturity.

expectations.text: The reply counts the full cost (such as licences or usage, integration, data work, controls, review and error handling), with estimates labelled.
expectations.evidence: 'AI programme cost in year 1 of SEK 12-18m (licences and usage, integration, data work, controls, monitoring, human review) and SEK 8-12m a year after that'. B also has 'Paid reskilling time', 'Backfill exceptions and temporary cover', 'Voluntary exit packages' and 'Extra attrition from change'. A has severance, transition and legal, contractors, rehiring and extra attrition. All marked '(est.)'. The AI cost is one lump with a listed scope, not itemised.

expectations.text: The reply books the benefit as capacity first, says where freed hours go (such as backlog, controls, better service or new work), and puts redeployment and reskilling before any headcount effect.
expectations.evidence: 'Hours freed are capacity first; they become savings only when they turn into roles that are not backfilled or that leave voluntarily.' 'Redeploy about 6 people into growing work: IFRS 17 and Solvency II reporting, DORA and internal-control work, data quality, and the reviewer roles the AI itself needs. Redeployment is not booked as a saving.' 'Offer redeployment and paid training first.' Voluntary exits only after Gate 2. Caveat: the model books freeze/attrition savings from Q1 whatever the AI delivers.

expectations.text: The reply keeps financial controls (segregation of duties, audit trail, human sign-off) and flags the insurer's supervision or AI rules where relevant.
expectations.evidence: 'Segregation of duties, audit trail and a human sign-off on payments and journals; internal audit and the external auditor involved before Gate 1.' 'DORA and outsourcing rules for any external AI provider; Solvency II governance and data-quality requirements; consult Finansinspektionen's expectations before relying on AI in regulated reporting.'

expectations.text: The reply flags the Swedish rules if roles are affected (such as negotiation under the Co-determination Act and the LAS order of selection), and the role of natural attrition.
expectations.evidence: 'Timeline: negotiation with the unions before the decision (MBL), notification to the Public Employment Service at least four months ahead (26-100 people)...'; 'Selection follows length of service (LAS) within each unit and collective agreement area, with room to exempt three people.' Attrition drives Option B: 'hiring freeze ... attrition 9% a year', with team size going 79 / 72 / 66.

expectations.text: The reply gives the board a staged plan with decision points and a recommendation, not a 30% headcount number.
expectations.evidence: 'Do not commit to removing 30% of the 90 roles next year.' Option B is recommended with 'Gate 1 (end Q2), Gate 2 (end Q4), Gate 3 (mid year 2): scale only what the measured results support', and decisions asked: 'Approve the gated programme and Year 1 budget of SEK 12.5m (est.), with Gates 1-3 as the only way further commitments are released.' Caveat: the headline still anchors on '27-30% by the end of year 3'.

overall_quality.evidence: The model reproduces the tables and sensitivities, and three gates plus IFRS 17/Solvency II redeployment are useful. But capacity is sized gross of review, the gated plan's savings don't depend on what the AI delivers (no low-capacity case for B), and the recommendation anchors on 27-30% by year 3.

factual_errors.evidence: No errors found in MBL, LAS and three exemptions, four months' notification for 26-100, 1-6 months' notice, nine months' re-employment priority, the 31.42% employer charges (model), or the MIT NANDA, Gartner and Orgvue figures.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of skills, reference files or ladder/rung jargon.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt has no bad outcome.

best_insight.value: The sensitivity shows AI run cost is the swing factor (30% cheaper gives break-even over three years, 30% dearer gives about -18m), and the stronger case is absorbing IFRS 17, Solvency II and DORA workload without proportional hiring.
best_insight.evidence: Board paper section 5, confirmed by model.py output

suggestions.reason: All six samples pass all six assertions, so the set doesn't separate the samples. Add one that checks the money: the recommended option's headcount reduction is capped by measured capacity, and the recommended option gets a low-capacity sensitivity. Sample D's gated plan books attrition savings whatever the AI delivers, and no assertion caught it.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the board a staged plan with decision points and a recommendation, not a 30% headcount number.
suggestions.reason: This passes a reply that anchors the board on a headcount percentage close to 30% at a later date (for example '27-30% by end of year 3' or 'targets a 15-30% reduction'). Consider requiring that the number the board commits to is set at a gate from measured results, not a target range given today.

suggestions.assertion: The reply counts the full cost (such as licences or usage, integration, data work, controls, review and error handling), with estimates labelled.
suggestions.reason: A single lump-sum 'AI programme' line with a list of what it covers passes as easily as an itemised build. Consider requiring that review and exception time is netted out of capacity or costed explicitly, and that the cost lines are itemised.

Sample D's Option B savings come from an 80% backfill freeze starting in Q1, before any gate, and don't change if the AI under-delivers. An assertion that headcount effects follow measured capacity would catch this.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions pass, but D shows they are lenient: its gated plan's savings are decoupled from AI capacity and it anchors on ~30% by year 3, and nothing caught either.
